inputs.share_count_basis: 11,611,774,184 shares (9,894.5m A + 1,717.2m H) per FY2025 AR p.1 and H1 FY2026 balance sheet; no options, no SBC scheme, the 2023 convertible bonds were fully converted (358m shares) — basic = fully diluted. Held FLAT. Note: the count rose 18% FY2020->FY2025 through consideration shares and A-share placements funding parent asset injections; future injections paid in shares are NOT modelled (assumed value-neutral at fair value) but are the main dilution risk.
inputs.total_debt_note: 30 Jun 2026 consolidated balance sheet: short-term loans 41,971 + non-current liabilities due within one year 19,427 + long-term loans 42,780 + bonds payable 23,994 + lease liabilities 880 + super short-term commercial papers 4,508 (inside 'other current liabilities'; MD&A s.10 lists them as borrowings) = 133,560. The Metrics.csv TotalDebt of 129,052 omits the SCP. MD&A cross-check: borrowings 95,715 + SCP 4,508 + MTN/PPN 32,314 + leases 1,011 = 133,548.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 OCF 27,220.6 less purchase of fixed/intangible/long-term assets 15,062.7. Under CAS interest paid sits in financing, so this OCF is pre-interest (unlevered), matching the engine. FY2025 OCF carried a ~5bn working-capital inflow (payables/contract liabilities as coal prices fell) that is not repeatable; the component build does not carry it forward (wc_capture 0).
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income on deposits 38.4m FY2025 (note V.50). Not deducted: the company is a net borrower (net debt 127.6bn), so the cash pile is not being added to EV.
inputs.sbc_source: none — state-owned enterprise with no share-award or option scheme (FY2025 AR directors' report, note V.40 lists only perpetual bonds as other equity instruments); SBC rows kept explicit at 0%
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1722, Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-11. All flows and per-share values are computed in RMB and multiplied by 1.1722 into HKD for comparison with the H-share price. Direction check: the Shanghai A-share (600027.SS) closed RMB5.19 on 2026-10-09 = HK$6.08 at this rate, against the H-share at HK$4.36 — a 28% H-discount, typical of the AH premium on SOE power names (not an FX error). refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate; re-check it on any later price refresh.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: 10y China Government Bond ~1.8% (Oct-2026). ERP 6.0% for China A/H equities, levered beta ~1.0 (unlevered utility beta ~0.5 relevered at ~1.4x D/E at market) -> cost of equity ~7.8%. Debt: FY2025 interest expense 3,249m on ~128bn average borrowings = 2.5% pre-tax, ~2.3% after tax at the 22% cash rate (state-bank SOE pricing); perpetual bonds carry 1.9-3.3% coupons (note V.40). Claims at market: ordinary 43bn + NCI 32bn (book) 33%, perpetuals 21bn 9%, debt 134bn 58% -> mechanical WACC 4.1-4.6%. House uses 5.0%: the 2026 trough in state-bank lending rates is not capitalised in perpetuity (through-cycle Kd ~3.0% pre-tax; FY2018-19 interest paid ran ~5%). The SAME 5.0% is used in all three scenarios — coal-spread, tariff-reform and dilution risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities 1,011m (880 non-current + ~131 current; MD&A s.10) are inside total_debt; no lease charge in the flows; right-of-use depreciation (immaterial) stays inside D&A and renewal inside capex. Leases are <1% of debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the bridge: non-controlling interests deducted at book, 31,979m at 30 Jun 2026 (32,926m at FY2025). NCI took 26% of FY2025 net profit (2,146m of 8,217m) and 26% in H1 FY2026; NCI holders contributed 4,607m of fresh capital in FY2025 and 5,301m in FY2024 while drawing 1,131m/2,050m of dividends, i.e. they co-fund the growth capex charged 100% in these flows. Book is the house default and the only auditable figure; it is harsh when the ordinary residual is near zero (minorities' plant stakes are then worth less than book too) — a proportional allocation (NCI = 26-39% of post-debt equity value) would lift the base value by roughly RMB2.5-3/share. Perpetual capital securities 21,002m (face; RMB 21.0bn of 2+N/3+N medium-term notes classified as other equity instruments) are also deducted in the bridge as a debt-like prior claim: their distributions (~1.0bn/yr) are paid out of equity and are not in the unlevered flows, so deducting face once is the single correct charge.
inputs.bridge_note: Matching-asset rule: income from associates and JVs (3,148m FY2025, 3,374m FY2024 restated, 1,261m H1 FY2026) is EXCLUDED from the EBITDA build (it sits below operating profit in the component build; OperatingProfitCAS 10,163m = EBIT 10,909m + investment income 3,153m - impairments 766m + other 38m - finance costs 3,162m, ties). Its source asset, long-term equity investments of 50,694m at 30 Jun 2026 (Huadian Coal Industry, Huadian Finance, Ningxia and ~20-50%-owned plant JVs), goes into the bridge AT VALUE: normalised associate income 3.0bn (average of FY2024r, FY2025 and annualised H1 FY2026) capitalised at the 7.8% cost of equity = 38,500m, 0.76x book, because these associates earn ~6% on book, below the cost of equity (coal-mine associates also fall as coal falls — a natural hedge to the 18% mid-cycle generation margin assumed). Carrying them at book instead would add 12,194m (~RMB1.05/share). Other equity-instrument investments 151m + other non-current financial assets 212m added at carrying value.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: non-US cyclical operating company, with the adaptations file applied — CNY WACC, lease treatment A, NCI and perpetuals in the bridge, associates under the matching-asset rule, SBC-zero market so house = street and band_position is null). FRESH BUILD, no prior DCF. ACCOUNTING BASIS: FY2025 is the first year on the post-common-control basis (80% of Huadian Jiangsu Energy + 7 entities injected by the parent, completed Jun-Jul 2025); FY2024 was restated from 112,392m to 141,502m revenue and the FY2025 -10.95% decline is on that restated basis. FY2018-FY2024 rows in Metrics.csv are the old scope and old HKFRS presentation, so historical CAGRs are not scope-consistent (see historical_growth.notes). FY2025 'OperatingIncome' is NULL in the CSV because the CAS line includes associate income and finance costs; the EBITDA used here is rebuilt from revenue less operating cost, taxes & surcharges, selling, admin and R&D, plus 'other income' (655m, mostly recurring VAT refunds/grants), plus D&A 13,142m = 24,051m (19.1%). Non-operating revenue (747m) and impairments are excluded. CAPEX SUPERCYCLE: FY2026 guidance RMB19bn (16.5% of revenue) against D&A ~12.9bn, for 10.8 GW under construction incl. ~4 GW pumped storage; the base path tapers capex to 12% of revenue (1.04x D&A) by FY2033, the AIA.NZ capex-supercycle-then-taper treatment. VERDICT SHAPE: on an owner-FCF basis the enterprise (EV ~106bn + associates ~39bn) is worth less than its prior claims (net debt 127.6bn + perpetuals 21.0bn + NCI 32.0bn = 180.6bn), so the ordinary equity is worth about zero or less in base and bear. That is the finding, not an artefact: the FY2025 dividend (2.7bn) plus perpetual coupons (1.0bn) plus NCI dividends (1.1bn) were paid while capex exceeded D&A by ~2bn and the company raised 22.5bn of new equity (consideration shares, A-share placement, NCI contributions) — distributions are funded by new capital and 2.5% state-bank debt, not by owner cash flow. The market price (0.87x ordinary book, 6.2% yield, ~8x P/E) is a dividend-yield-and-carry valuation that requires the 2.5% debt cost to persist and the cap on the terminal multiple to be ignored: it reconciles only at ~4.3% WACC with an uncapped Gordon terminal. PRICE: the H-share print is a regular Friday close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward base-case driver path (FY2026 guidance of ~240m MWh vs 262m in FY2025, then capacity additions); 10-year average of the base growth path is ~0.8%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are not scope-consistent: FY2025 is on the post-Jiangsu-injection basis (FY2024 restated +26% to 141.5bn) while FY2020-FY2024 rows are the old scope, so the 7.1% revenue CAGR is mostly acquisition. Equity CAGR (ordinary, ex-perpetuals: 48.5bn FY2020 -> 48.2bn FY2025) is -0.1% while the share count rose 18% (9,863m -> 11,612m), so ordinary book value PER SHARE compounded at -3.3%/yr. EPS 5yr 8.3% diverges >30% from equity -0.1%: the EPS gain is a coal-price-cycle recovery (FY2021-22 losses), not compounding. 3-year EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative FY2022 base); the 5-year owner-FCF CAGR of 49% is from a 1.6bn trough and includes FY2025's ~5bn working-capital inflow — not meaningful.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF throughout (SBC 0, interest income not stripped as the company is a net borrower). Owner-FCF series FY2020-FY2025 (m): 1,632 / -23,596 / -5,004 / -1,029 / 3,823 / 12,158 — a coal-spread cycle, not a trend. Dividends per share: FY2025 RMB0.23 (interim 0.09 + final 0.14), FY2024 RMB0.21; H1 FY2026 interim RMB0.09 declared despite -20% profit.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026: guided generation ~240m MWh vs 262.27m in FY2025 (-8.5%), H1 FY2026 revenue -9.5% with tariff +0.2% and heat +; FY2027-32 +1-2%: Wangting 2x660MW, new gas units and the first pumped-storage units come on line and the coal capacity payment steps from ~30% to >=50% of fixed costs, against continued erosion of thermal utilisation hours (3,427h in FY2025, -378h); fade to 1.5% as the thermal fleet loses dispatch share.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA 19.1% and H1 FY2026 21.0% were earned at RMB834/t standard coal, the low end of the RMB700-900/t range forecast for 2026; FY2024 restated was 15.6%, FY2023 12.6%, FY2018-20 19-23%, FY2021-22 -3% to +6%. 18% mid-cycle assumes the post-2022 tariff float (+/-20% around benchmark) and the capacity payment keep the cycle shallower than 2021-22 but that spot-market rollout caps the upside.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guidance ~RMB19bn (16.5% of revenue) for 10,818 MW approved/under construction including ~4 GW pumped storage; tapers to 12% (1.04x D&A) by FY2033 as that wave completes. Terminal capex is held near D&A because the terminal value is bound by the 20x cap, which gives no credit for growth capex beyond maintenance.
base.tax_rationale: Statutory 25% (15% western-China subsidiaries); FY2025 income tax 2,431m on EBIT ex-associates 10,909m = 22.3%; current tax alone 1,650m (15%). No group relief in the PRC, so loss-making plants do not shelter profitable ones — 22% on EBIT.
base.wacc_rationale: 5.0% CNY — see inputs.wacc_rationale. Gordon at 5.0%/1.5% is 29x terminal FCF; the 20x cap binds (terminal EV/EBITDA ~4.6x vs ~7-8x where Chinese IPPs trade — the cap is conservative by design and the uncapped memo value is in valuation_philosophy).
base.narrative: Thermal dispatch keeps eroding at 1-2%/yr in volume, offset by capacity payments and the gas/pumped-storage build; coal stays in the RMB700-900/t band so the generation spread settles at an 18% EBITDA margin; the FY2026-28 capex wave completes and capex tapers to maintenance; the parent keeps injecting assets at roughly fair value in shares (value-neutral, not modelled). Owner FCF runs 1.8-6bn/yr on 115-134bn of revenue. The enterprise is worth less than its net debt plus perpetuals plus minorities, so the ordinary equity is worth about zero: the dividend is being funded by new capital and cheap state-bank debt.

bull.narrative: Capacity payments rise to >=50-70% of fixed costs and stick; coal stays at or below RMB800/t while the tariff float holds, so the H1 FY2026 21% margin becomes the run-rate at 20%; the pumped-storage and gas additions and heat growth lift volumes 2.5-3%/yr from FY2027; the gas-turbine REIT model is replicated so growth is funded by asset recycling rather than placements and capex falls to ~1.05x D&A by FY2030; associates (Huadian Coal, Huadian Finance) keep earning ~3bn. Even here the ordinary residual is thin — the bull case is the one in which the equity has positive value at all.

bear.narrative: The 2026 spot-market rollout and renewables' low marginal cost push realised tariffs down faster than capacity payments rise; utilisation hours keep falling (volume -3%/-1% in FY2027-28 then flat); coal mean-reverts toward RMB900/t so the margin settles at the FY2024 restated level (15.5%); the state-directed build programme does not taper (capex 13-16% of revenue, well above D&A, on regulated returns below the cost of capital), loss-making plants get no tax relief (25%), and buyers de-rate stranded thermal (15x cap, 0.5% terminal growth). A further parent injection paid in discounted shares would make this worse still; it is not in the numbers. Equity is deeply negative on an owner-FCF basis: the shares are an option on rates and tariffs, not a claim on cash flow.

scenario_narratives.base: Owner FCF is rebuilt from components on the restated FY2025 base: revenue falls 8.5% in FY2026 on the ~240m MWh guidance, then grows 1-2% as gas, pumped-storage and capacity payments offset thermal erosion; EBITDA settles at an 18% mid-cycle margin (between FY2025's 19.1% coal-trough year and FY2024's restated 15.6%); the FY2026 RMB19bn capex wave tapers to ~1.04x D&A by FY2033; 22% cash tax; 5.0% CNY WACC; 1.5% terminal growth with the 20x FCF cap binding. Associates are carried at 38.5bn (income capitalised at CoE), perpetuals (21.0bn) and NCI (32.0bn, book) are deducted after net debt of 127.6bn. The enterprise is worth roughly 30-40bn less than those prior claims, so the ordinary equity is worth about zero in base: the 6% dividend yield is financed by placements, parent consideration shares, minority contributions and 2.5% state-bank debt rather than by free cash flow.
scenario_narratives.bull: Capacity payments and a RMB700-800/t coal band hold the margin at 20%, volumes grow 2.5-3% on the clean-energy build, growth is funded by REIT recycling so capex falls to 1.05x D&A, and the terminal growth is 2.5%. This is the only path in which the ordinary residual is positive, and even then only modestly so.
scenario_narratives.bear: Spot-market tariff compression and renewables' dispatch priority outrun the capacity payment; coal mean-reverts to ~RMB900/t and the margin settles at 15.5%; the state-directed build does not taper (capex 13%+ of revenue at sub-WACC regulated returns), losses at individual plants get no group tax relief, and buyers de-rate thermal to a 15x cap. Equity is deeply negative; holders are relying on the parent and the state banks, not on cash flow.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: a single customer (State Grid 77% of sales) and a single regulator set both the tariff and the fuel-cost pass-through; the thermal fleet is in structural decline as renewables take dispatch; leverage is 58% of EV at floating rates; and governance runs through connected-party injections that dilute at the parent's discretion (share count +18% in five years). Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to hold at once — coal staying in the low band, capacity payments stepping up and sticking, the capex wave actually tapering, and no further discounted issuance. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: An owner-FCF DCF of a 58%-levered state-owned thermal generator in a capex build-out, with the prior claims (net debt, perpetual notes, minorities) deducted at face and the associates added at value. The result — ordinary equity worth about zero or less in base and bear — is the honest output of asking what cash this business generates for its ordinary holders after growth capex and prior claims, discounted at a CNY rate built from the flows' own currency. The market values the H-shares as a yield instrument (0.87x ordinary book, 6.2% dividend yield, ~8x P/E, EV/EBITDA ~8.6x including associate income); that price reconciles to a DCF only at ~4.3% WACC with an uncapped Gordon terminal, associates at book and no haircut on the capital raised to pay the dividend. Memo values on the base path: uncapped Gordon at 5.0%/1.5% lifts the base by ~RMB2.9/share to roughly zero; associates at book add ~RMB1.05/share; a proportional NCI allocation adds ~RMB2.5-3/share; a dividend-discount cross-check (RMB0.23 growing 1.5% at a 7.8% CoE) gives ~RMB3.7 = HK$4.3, i.e. the current price, and is what the market is doing. House basis equals street basis (no SBC); band_position is null.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: the equity is the residual of ~145bn of value against ~181bn of prior claims, so every 0.5pp of WACC moves the value by roughly RMB1-1.5/share; the mechanical CNY WACC (4.1-4.6%) is below the 5.0% used and the market is pricing ~4.3%.
Terminal multiple: the 20x FCF cap binds (Gordon 29x at 5%/1.5%); it is equivalent to ~4.6x terminal EV/EBITDA against 6-8x for listed Chinese IPPs. Uncapped, base is ~zero rather than negative.

Capex taper: the base assumes the RMB19bn FY2026 programme falls to ~1.04x D&A by FY2033; if the state keeps directing growth capex at regulated returns below the cost of capital (bear), owner FCF never emerges.
Coal spread: every 1pp of EBITDA margin is ~1.3bn of EBITDA (~RMB1/share at the terminal multiple); FY2025-H1 FY2026 margins were earned at trough coal prices.

Dilution: 1,384m shares were issued in FY2025 for the Jiangsu injection and ancillary funding; further parent injections paid in shares at a discount to value are the main per-share risk and are not in the paths.

NCI and perpetuals: deducted at book/face (53bn, 29% of claims); a proportional allocation of a near-zero residual would be far less punitive — the choice is the house default, not a finding about the minorities' value.

Associates: 50.7bn book (38.5bn used) earns ~6% on book from coal-mining and finance affiliates whose profits halved in H1 FY2026; a hard fall in coal helps the generation margin and hurts the associates — the two are partially hedged.
